Write short notes (design choices, what you could not do and why) to /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/story-ending-notes/notes.md (create the directory).

OWNED FILES: storygame/story_package/models.py, storygame/story_package/loader.py, storygame/runtime/state.py, storygame/runtime/engine.py, storygame/runtime/attempt_bundle.py (additive field only, schema_version stays 1), storygame/web_demo.py, tests/test_story_ending.py (new), and any existing test you must update because behaviour legitimately changed (say which in notes). Edit nothing else.

GOAL: the engine has no concept of the story ending. After the last scene's final reveal the game just waits for more input. Add a story-agnostic, data-driven ending: an authored closing beat shown once, after which the game is complete and no further narration is requested (no model call, no billing).

READ FIRST: storygame/story_package/models.py (ScenePacing, Transition, FactPredicate, the pacing document class that holds `transitions`), storygame/story_package/loader.py (how pacing is loaded and validated; how cue_text and other authored player text is safety-checked), storygame/runtime/state.py (RuntimeState, RuntimeSnapshot, snapshot/restore), storygame/runtime/engine.py (turn flow: where a turn is committed, where handoff and authored cue/transition segments are appended, how a rejected turn restores its snapshot), storygame/runtime/attempt_bundle.py, storygame/web_demo.py (session and turn responses, _state_summary-like dict that includes pending_game_break), tests/test_attempt_bundle.py, tests/test_cue_escalation.py, tests/test_design_review_fixtures.py (how to build a real engine state).

BUILD:
1. models.py: new frozen model `StoryEnding` with `scene_id` (scene id pattern), `when: tuple[FactPredicate, ...]` (min_length 1), `text: str` (non-empty, stripped) and `marker: str` (non-empty, one line). The pacing document gets `ending: StoryEnding | None = None`. Packages without it behave exactly as today.
2. loader.py: validate that ending.scene_id is a known scene, that every `when` fact id is a known fact (use the same check transitions use), that the ending scene has no outgoing transition (a scene that leads elsewhere cannot be the ending), and apply to `text` and `marker` the same player-safety scan the loader applies to cue_text (an ending may not contain a protected or guarded term unless the loader's existing rule allows it at that point; follow what cue_text does).
3. state.py: add `story_complete: bool = False` to RuntimeState and RuntimeSnapshot (old snapshots and saves load with False). Include it in snapshot creation and restore, so a rejected attempt can never complete the story.
4. engine.py: after a turn is committed and after any handoff delivery, authored cue and scene-transition processing for that turn, if package.pacing.ending is set, the current scene equals ending.scene_id, every `when` predicate holds in the committed facts, and story_complete is False: append ONE authored segment with ending.text as the LAST segment of the turn, set story_complete True, and record it. It is appended through the same authored path as handoff delivery, never generated by the narrator and never put in a narrator prompt. If a forced handoff on the same turn delivers the fact that satisfies `when`, the ending still fires on that same turn, after the handoff text. A rejected or game-break turn must not fire it (snapshot restore handles this; test it). Once story_complete is True, any further turn must return a fixed response containing ending.marker without calling the provider, advancing the turn index or changing facts. State this as a distinct, documented result type, not an error.
5. attempt_bundle.py: add an additive optional field `story_complete: bool = False` recorded on every attempt path (true on the turn that completed the story and on any later no-op turn). Keep schema_version 1; old bundles load.
6. web_demo.py: the turn response and the session/state summary expose `story_complete` (bool) and, when true, `ending_marker` (string). The no-op turn after completion returns HTTP 200 with the marker and story_complete true, and makes no provider or semantic call (assert in a test with a provider that raises if called). Make sure the existing rate limits and the FREYTAG_EXPOSE_PROMPT gate behave as before.
7. Tests in tests/test_story_ending.py, hermetic (no network), real engine state with stubbed providers, under 20 s. Build the ending with package.model_copy on a real package (do not edit data/): scene 3C, when phase_two_conflict_plan_known equals true, text 'Test closing paragraph.', marker 'The story ends here.'. Cases: (a) ending fires exactly once on the turn the fact becomes true, as the last segment, with story_complete true in state and bundle; (b) not before the fact; (c) not in another scene; (d) rejected attempt on that turn: not fired, state restored, fires on the next accepted turn; (e) forced handoff turn that delivers the fact fires the ending after the handoff text; (f) after completion a further turn makes no provider call, does not advance turn_index and returns the marker; (g) snapshot round trip and an old snapshot without story_complete load; (h) a package without `ending` is unchanged; (i) loader refuses unknown scene, unknown fact, a scene with an outgoing transition, and an empty text; (j) web layer: the turn response carries story_complete and ending_marker; the following request is a 200 no-op with no provider call.
8. Hard rules: story-agnostic (no 3C or Continuity-specific branches in storygame/), no network, no fact changes after rendering, plain comments matching surrounding style, narrator-facing strings: you add none.

HOW TO RUN: confirm `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c "import storygame; print(storygame.__file__)"` prints a path inside the cwd. Tests: PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_story_ending.py, then the full suite with -n auto. Ruff: PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check --fix . and -m ruff format . . Reply with the files changed.
